derating.closed_form: ratio = sum_c E_c / (max_c dur_c * sum_c s_c) = (s-weighted mean duration) / (max duration); the longest-duration cohort binds; ratio = 1 iff all active durations equal

soc_excursion.derivation:
Under H3 (pnet_c = share_c * agg, share by INSTALLED E) and aggregate SoC limits [0.1, 0.9] x available energy
    (start / closure 0.5), the aggregate stored-energy excursion from the start is <= 0.4 sum_k E_k SoH_k; cohort c
    moves share_c of it, i.e. <= 0.4 E_c (sum_k E_k SoH_k / sum_k E_k); relative to its OWN available energy E_c SoH_c
    the bound is 0.4 r_c with r_c = SoH_bar_E / SoH_c. The oldest cohort has r > 1: its implied SoC range
    0.5 +- 0.4 r exceeds its own [0.1, 0.9] by (r - 1). SoH calendar-only, END of block (the 'end' available energy).

what_a_common_base_draw_twin_needs: per network block, the pool-row selection of the BASE key (2025, day) for every year: the block seed derive_random_seed(network_seed, 'realization', 2025, day) instead of (year, day), hence every per-load / per-generator sample (pc, qc, pc_flex, pc_flex_up, pc_flex_down, pg, qg) draws the same pool rows as 2025
market: derive_random_seed(market_seed, 'selection', 'energy' | 'flexibility', 2025, day) for every year

growth then applied by production with the TRUE year: loads (1 + g_load)^(year - 2025) on pc, qc; (1 + g_flex_load)^(year - 2025) on pc_flex, pc_flex_up, pc_flex_down; market (1 + g_energy)^(year - 2025) and (1 + g_flexibility)^(year - 2025); RES pg / qg scaled by the YEAR network file capacity (Pmax), no growth factor

because pd = (pc + pc_flex) / baseMVA mixes two growth rates (g_load != g_flex_load on every network), the twin cannot be made by rescaling the final pd arrays post read: it needs the re-keyed draw at generation (a pass-through wrapper on derive_random_seed in network_data / shared_resources_planning mapping the 'realization' and 'selection' labels' year to 2025, or an equivalent pre-checksum injection of arrays computed from the 2025 draws with separate pc / pc_flex growth)

the synthetic pools (KDE, 100 samples per day) are already year-free and shared by both grids: their seeds derive from (network seed, 'synthetic_profiles') and (market seed, 'synthetic_profiles') only
the twin changes the scenario checksum; the prefix / EV / checksum pins would be new artefacts (a scenario-construction decision, A5)
twin_scoping.shared_draws_between_grids: 2025 only (draw keys equal and arrays bitwise equal); every other year uses distinct (year, day) keys; the year-free KDE pools are common to both grids
